title: Prime Lanterns
statement: A festival hangs lanterns on poles numbered 2 to n − 1 and lights only the poles whose number is prime. Return how many lanterns are lit, that is, how many prime numbers are less than `n`.

keyPoints: Start with every number from 2 to n − 1 marked as possibly prime
For each p from 2 while p * p < n: if p is still marked, cross out p*p, p*p + p, ... below n
Starting at p * p works because smaller multiples were crossed out by smaller primes
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Test each number by trial division up to its square root: O(n √n), too slow for 5 million

hints: Checking each number on its own repeats a lot of work. What can one prime tell you about many other numbers?
Every multiple of a prime p (other than p) is not prime. Cross them out.
Use a boolean array; for p with p * p < n, if p is unmarked, cross out from p * p in steps of p. Count the rest.
